abstract: Selecting peptides candidates for target proteomics requires integrating a multicriteria problem, particularly when users lack prior experimental data, programming expertise, or stable access to external repositories. We development SeekNSee, a locally executed R/Shiny application designed to improve the reproducibility and auditability of peptide-candidate screening through enzyme-aware in silico digestion, configurable and traceable rule-level decision tracking. Starting from a user provided reference proteome and target sequences, SeekNSee generates peptides-candidates using nine digestion configurations and evaluates them with 12 rules configured as ignore, apply, or block. Numerical score and retained/blocking status are stored independently, and every candidate-rule outcome is preserved in a rule-level trace. Computational validation confirmed the specified behavior in controlled cases through 198 passing automated assertions, complemented by successful operational and processing tests on Windows and Ubuntu. Proteome-wide application covered all 20,416 reviewed human proteins, generating 733,864 peptide-candidate and 581,026 unique peptides sequences while preserving data integrity, decision traceability, and candidate-specific context. DIA, DDA, and deep-fractionated proteomics benchmarking showed strong associations between SeekNSee scores categories, peptide observation, and multiple analytical measurements. Together, these results support that SeekNSee provides a transparent and traceable screening layer for generating peptide-candidates for subsequent assay and experimental validation.
